### 2.1 p-n Junction Diode & Zener Diode Regulation (Semiconductor Diodes)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **46 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Forward and reverse characteristics of p-n junctions, rectifiers, ripple frequency, and Zener diode shunt voltage stabilization.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{Efficiency}_{\text{half-wave}} = 40.6\%, \quad \text{Efficiency}_{\text{full-wave}} = 81.2\%, \quad V_L = V_Z = \text{const}, \quad I_S = I_Z + I_L
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: In full-wave rectifiers, output ripple frequency is TWICE the AC input frequency ($2f_{\text{in}}$), whereas for half-wave it is $f_{\text{in}}$.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: In reverse breakdown, Zener diode maintains constant voltage $V_Z$ across its terminals as long as $I_Z \ge I_{Z,\text{min}}$.

### 2.2 Logic Gates & Truth Tables (Digital Electronics)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **46 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Universal logic gates (NAND and NOR), De Morgan's theorems, and Boolean circuit reduction.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{NAND: } Y = \overline{A \cdot B}, \quad \text{NOR: } Y = \overline{A + B}, \quad \overline{A \cdot B} = \overline{A} + \overline{B}, \quad \overline{A + B} = \overline{A} \cdot \overline{B}
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: NAND and NOR gates are UNIVERSAL gates: any Boolean function can be constructed using only NAND or only NOR gates.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Connect inputs of a NAND or NOR gate together to obtain a NOT gate: $\overline{A \cdot A} = \overline{A}$.

#### Linked Representative PYQs:
- **[2026 Evening Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"$\text{The output}Y\text{for the given inputs}A\text{and}B\text{to the circuit is :}$..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

- **[2026 Evening Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"If X and Y are the inputs, the given circuit works as _________...."* — **Correct Answer: D**
- **[2026 Evening Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"$\text{Identify the correct truth table of the given logic circuit.}$..."* — **Correct Answer: A**

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring JEE Mains Pitfalls in Semiconductor Syllabus reduced

### 1. Sign Convention & Vector Inversion Errors
Paper-setters frequently exploit sign confusion in energy and potential differences. Always write the fundamental thermodynamic / vector definition before substituting numerical values.

### 2. Unit System Discrepancies
Molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), SI vs CGS units, and micro/milli/nano multipliers (10^-3, 10^-6, 10^-9) account for over 35% of calculation mistakes in numerical type questions.

### 3. Boundary & Extreme Conditions
In transient circuits or limiting conditions (t=0+, t -> inf, infinite dilution, resonance), always check the asymptotic behavior of inductors, capacitors, and electrolyte mobility.

### 4. Direct Addition Fallacy
Never algebraically add intensive quantities (such as electrode potentials or AC component voltages) without accounting for electron weighting (n1*E1 + n2*E2 = n3*E3) or phasor vector geometry (V_total = sqrt(V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2)).
